_doc: Curated technique seeds (knowledge_architecture.md section 5), one file per area. Fields: id, level + scope (a scope node or universal), aliases (v1 / technique-DB / footer names folded in), mechanism, preconditions (predicate DSL), predicts (canonical metric -> up|down|flat|up_or_flat|down_or_flat), risks (pitfalls), states / op_classes / op_kinds gates (empty = any), slot (offered by the multi-slot agent), prior {mean, n}: a seed prior with a low pseudo-count that evidence overrides, realizations by scope (target:<key> | target:<backend>:sm_NN+ | target:<backend> | node:<id> | universal). Loaded by Ontology.seed(); scripts/seed_knowledge.py builds a knowledge.db from these files.

techniques.mechanism: read-heavy 2D operands through image2d_t: the texture path has its own L1 and handles 2D locality and boundary clamping
risks: image formats (CL_RGBA, CL_FLOAT / CL_HALF_FLOAT) pack 4 channels per texel; width limits (16384)
the driver must create the image; slots that only get buffers can use cl_khr_image2d_from_buffer

realizations.how: Weights / activations as image2d_t (RGBA: 4 channels per texel) read with read_imagef(img, sampler, (int2)(x, y)); outputs stay buffers.

techniques.mechanism: on Adreno __local is not much faster than the L1/texture path and costs barriers: block in registers first and use local memory only for real cross-work-item reuse
risks: register pressure lowers the kernel's max work-group size

realizations.how: Each work-item computes a 4x4 (float4 x 4) output block from vload4 rows read directly from global / image memory; add __local tiling only if profiling shows repeated global reads.

techniques.mechanism: pin the subgroup to a full (or half) 64-wide wave so subgroup reductions and broadcasts map to one wave
Adreno ALUs run half at twice the float rate: elementwise and activation math in half / half4 where the tolerance allows
risks: fp32 problems: half intermediate rounding (~1e-3) can exceed the bound; accumulate reductions in float

realizations.how: #pragma OPENCL EXTENSION cl_khr_fp16 : enable; vload_half4 / convert_half4 for the math, float accumulators for sums.

techniques.mechanism: fused multiply-add instructions instead of separate multiply and add

realizations.how: fmaf / __fmaf_rn in inner products (nvcc contracts by default unless --fmad=false).

techniques.mechanism: read / write fp16 data as half4 / half8 vectors straight through the half pointer (one 64 / 128-bit transaction per work-item), 8 elements per work-item
risks: alignment of vload8 is per element, but a scalar tail is needed for n % 8
fewer work-items: keep the grid large enough to fill the GPU

realizations.how: vload8(0, x + i) / vstore8(v, 0, y + i) on __global half * with #pragma OPENCL EXTENSION cl_khr_fp16 : enable (the runtime prepends it); not vload_half.

techniques.mechanism: keep the data and the multiplies in fp16 but accumulate dot products in float (QNN's HYBRID mode): exact products, no accumulation drift
risks: convert_float8 on every weight vector costs ALU; hoist conversions out of inner loops

realizations.how: acc = mad((float8)((float)x), convert_float8(vload8(0, w)), acc) per tap; one convert_half8 on store.

techniques.mechanism: accumulate in half8 (2x ALU rate, no conversions) and flush the partial sums into float accumulators every 16-32 terms, bounding the fp16 summation error
risks: the per-slot bound (about two fp16 ulps) can fail on long dot products: rel_err 1.5e-3 against 2e-3 on a 576-term conv (flush 16), 2.4e-3 over 9 terms in one session
measured equal or slower than fp32 accumulation in all four sessions plus the seed (71 vs 65 ms; 5.2 vs 2.9 ms); a half fma() is emulated and ~80x slower than an fp32 mad

realizations.how: half8 h = mad((half8)(x), w8, h); every MB_ACC_FLUSH-th tap: acc += convert_float8(h); h = 0 (mb_opencl_kernels_f16_math.cpp, -DMB_ACC_HALF=1).

techniques.mechanism: one work-item computes 4 output pixels x 8 output channels in float8 accumulators with weights re-laid out [tap][OC] once per call and read as half8: input and weight loads are amortised over 32 mads
risks: registers lower the kernel's max work-group size (see MB_KINFO wg_max)
needs a weight re-layout kernel per call or a cached copy

realizations.how: k_wpack: wt[(ic*KH*KW + kh*KW + kw)*OCp + oc] (OC padded to the tile); k_conv over (ow/4, oh, n*OCp/OT). A 3x3 conv went from 3.7 GFLOP/s (seed) / 5-32 (flow finals) to ~50-70 GFLOP/s this way (QNN: 330-900); OT = 4 was 1.8x faster at IC = 8, OT = 8 1.6x faster at IC = 64 (cc_runs REPORTs).

techniques.mechanism: pack weights / a staged input into a slot-owned buffer and read it through an image2d view (cl_khr_image2d_from_buffer): texture-path cache and cl_qcom_accelerated / vector image ops
risks: rows are padded to the device pitch alignment (mb_image.pitch_bytes)
an extra pack kernel per call

realizations.how: mb_image im = MB_SCRATCH_IMAGE(cl_x, 0, w, h, CL_RGBA, CL_HALF_FLOAT); pack kernel writes im.buf as __global half *, the compute kernel takes im.img as image2d_t and calls read_imageh(img, smp, (int2)(x, y)).

techniques.mechanism: relaxed math build options let the compiler reassociate, fuse and flush denormals
risks: reassociates the compensated mb_kadd sums and breaks NaN / inf handling

realizations.how: MB_CL_OPTS("-cl-fast-relaxed-math", src), or -cl-unsafe-math-optimizations / -cl-finite-math-only / -cl-denorms-are-zero one at a time.

techniques.mechanism: fold BatchNorm scale/shift, bias, ReLU and the residual add into the convolution's store epilogue (what QNN does): fewer launches and DRAM round trips
risks: only where the graph optimiser accepted a fusion hint for the chain
keep the unfused stages' semantics bit-compatible

realizations.how: apply scale[c] * acc + shift[c] and max(.,0) / += residual on the float accumulators before convert_half and vstore.
